prior_identity_evidence.scope: Previous identity, host body-race failure and initial native stalled-response failure remain immutable. This run repeats all those passing semantic scopes; no historical failure is reclassified.

findings.boundary: A distinct nonroot socket principal sends identical direct attack POSTs to the owned HTTP and verified HTTPS backends. Open/rollback controls return 200 and independently record exact attack bytes/authority. Protected/reprotected sockets fail immediately before TLS/HTTP with zero backend effects; client timeout is not admitted as protection.
findings.inspection: The actual native-built identity-enabled CLI retains the same 44 normal-CRS ingress, benign body, attack denial, authority, metadata, health and recovery outcomes while backend restrictions are active. The allowed lab UID has positive backend states; deny counters independently witness foreign sockets.
findings.ownership: Root owns fixed policy selection, snapshots, invalid replacement and label-specific state removal. Public atomic marker/CA exchange between UID 32767 and UID 1 cannot select root commands, targets or policy. Private TLS keys stay in fixture-owned private temporary files. Both children are joined and public assets removed before phase transition.
findings.compatibility: All prior semantic controls and original sender-only policies remain unchanged. No non-test Go or dependency change; native companion/checker output hashes match the prior identity study.
findings.rollback: Invalid replacement preserves known good. Open rollback restores the same direct bypass effects; protected-again blocks them again. All three PF matrices independently restore eight static views before authenticated source/base invariance and VM teardown.

limitations: Conditional fresh loopback IPv4 sockets to two fixed owned lab backend ports only. The allowed companion/fixture UID is a test identity; compromise of that UID, root or PF administrators is outside this boundary.

This is not remote backend network isolation, an appliance firewall, production accounts/startup policy, cryptographic proxy authentication, IPv6 or existing-state/effect revocation. Other isolated lab traffic remains reachable.

The native foreign principal is the existing daemon account solely for testing. It is not a selected runtime account or service. Public synchronization is test-only and is not an appliance management API.

No Caddy rerun, comparative resource/soak acceptance, full CRS/OWASP coverage, protocol/streaming parity, certificate/audit policy, original image/installed-daemon lineage or product adoption. Prior Caddy advisory residuals remain.

Native execution has no race instrumentation; host Go/race/cross/advisory checks are separate tooling evidence. No live network, persistent service, installer schema or release changes. Private keys, raw logs and full source inventories remain ignored.
scope: Bounded local backend socket-UID isolation research with distinct-principal bypass attempts and independent effects, separate from production/network policy adoption.
